html:
The Tapieté and the Guaraní Ñandeva are related Tupi-Guarani speaking peoples of the western Gran Chaco, where Paraguay, Bolivia and Argentina meet. Unlike most Guaraní, they live in the dry thorn forest of the Chaco.

They grow maize and other crops where they can and also hunt, fish and gather. Their neighbours include the Ayoreo, Nivaclé and Wichí. The Chaco War of 1932 to 1935 split them across the new border and drove many to Paraguayan missions and ranches. Their language is close to that of the Guaraní east of the Paraguay river.
